newsitem.title: USA: AMR may post charge for Canadian Airlines stake.
newsitem.headline: AMR may post charge for Canadian Airlines stake.

text.p: AMR Corp may post a charge against 1996 earnings for the decline in market value of its investment in Canadian Airlines Corp, AMR spokesman Al Becker said Wednesday.
AMR originally invested $177 million in Canadian Airlines in 1994. The market value of that investment grew to $192 million with dividends but has now declined to $32 million, Becker said.
"If at some point that decline is not recoverable, then we are obligated to take a charge against earnings," Becker said. "We still need to determine how much of a charge."
While the company has not yet decided whether a charge will be necessary, it alerted shareholders of a possible charge in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Becker said.
The parent of American Airlines holds a one-third economic interest in Canadian Airlines and a 25 percent voting interest, Becker said.
AMR said it remains committed to its stake in Canadian Airlines and will maintain its marketing and code sharing relationship with the Calgary-based airline.
AMR collects about $100 million annually from Canadian Airlines by providing reservation services, computer and management information services, Becker said.
"All of those relationships will continue," Becker said.
Canandian Airlines, which has faced pressure from rising fuel costs and discount competitors, is expected to make a corporate announcement following a board meeting on Friday.
A Canadian Airlines spokeswoman told Reuters Tuesday that the company is mulling ways to improve profitability, but declined to comment on market rumors of employee pay cuts.
